english: Let $O$ be the origin of the Argand plane and let $OBCD$ be a square whose vertices $O,B,C,D$ are in the anticlockwise order. The vertex $B$ lies on the circle $|z-3-i|=\sqrt{5}$ and the vertex $D$ lies on the line $z+\bar{z}+4=0$, where $i=\sqrt{-1}$. If $C$ represents the complex number $c$, then the product of all possible values of $\mathrm{Re}(c)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $O$ आर्गण्ड तल का मूल बिन्दु है तथा $OBCD$ एक वर्ग है जिसके शीर्ष $O,B,C,D$ वामावर्त (anticlockwise) क्रम में हैं। शीर्ष $B$ वृत्त $|z-3-i|=\sqrt{5}$ पर स्थित है तथा शीर्ष $D$ रेखा $z+\bar{z}+4=0$ पर स्थित है, जहाँ $i=\sqrt{-1}$ है। यदि $C$ सम्मिश्र संख्या $c$ को निरूपित करता है, तो $\mathrm{Re}(c)$ के सभी सम्भव मानों का गुणनफल ______ है।
solution: Anticlockwise square: $D$ is $B$ rotated about $O$ through $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, so $d=ib$ ($e^{i\pi/2}=i$), and $c=b+d=(1+i)b$
solution_full: Let $B,C,D$ represent $b,c,d$. In the square $OBCD$ taken anticlockwise, $\overrightarrow{OD}$ is $\overrightarrow{OB}$ turned through $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ anticlockwise, so $d=e^{i\pi/2}b=ib$, with $|d|=|b|$.
The fourth vertex satisfies $c=b+d$ (the diagonals of a square bisect each other), so $c=(1+i)b$.

Since $|b-(3+i)|=\sqrt{5}$, multiplying by $i$ (a rotation, which keeps moduli): $|ib-i(3+i)|=\sqrt{5}$, i.e. $|d-(-1+3i)|=\sqrt{5}$. So $D$ lies on the circle with centre $-1+3i$ and radius $\sqrt{5}$.
Both give genuine squares ($b\neq0$). The possible values of $\mathrm{Re}(c)$ are $-1$ and $3$, with product $-3$.
originality_note: New: the rotation that carries B to D also carries the circle of B to a circle, which is intersected with the line of D (way 3, an object fixed by two conditions on different vertices). Closest known: square or equilateral triangle with one vertex at the origin and another on a given curve. Different because: two vertices carry two different conditions, so the rotated locus has to be intersected with the second condition, giving two squares.
